sourceBreakdown.quiet: PROVISIONAL ESTIMATE derived from Norwich International Airport (NWI): its two runway 09/27 final approaches as published in the UK AIP, sampled at 1 km. NOT sampled from DEFRA, which publishes no Round 4 surface for this airport. The distance ladder is calibrated on Heathrow and floored at the smallest airport DEFRA maps, so it reaches further than Norwich really does and the estimate is PESSIMISTIC. No departure routes are drawn because Norwich publishes no SIDs in the AIP at all, as at Teesside. Indicative only. The geometry estimate's flight routes and runway alignments (NWI) are derived by Sky Score from the UK Aeronautical Information Publication (NATS), and are not for navigation.
sourceBreakdown.afford: HM Land Registry UK House Price Index, August 2026 vintage, Open Government Licence v3.0. Methodology v5.0 scores this on a LOG scale against the 5th-95th percentile of borough medians across ALL 97 boroughs in the sterling pool (GBP 159,100 to GBP 732,271), not against this city cohort. Affordability is therefore comparable BETWEEN cities: a cheaper borough always scores higher than a dearer one, which within-city min-max did not deliver - it inverted 1,619 of the 4,371 cross-city borough pairs. context.priceRankInCity carries the within-city standing that scaling used to imply.
sourceBreakdown.live: 3 of 4 inputs measured. ONS Crime in England and Wales, Table C4; NaPTAN rail, metro and tram access within 800 m; NHS Organisation Data Service GP practices within 500 m. Absent inputs have their weight redistributed across the measured ones rather than being defaulted to a mid value, and context.liveResolution reports the count per response.
sourceBreakdown.env: Air quality (0.45), Road noise (0.35), Flood risk (0.20). Weights are re-normalised over the inputs a borough actually has; a borough below the two-input floor omits the component entirely.
sourceBreakdown.growth: HM Land Registry UK House Price Index, August 2026 vintage, 12-month price trend deflated by ONS CPIH (3.3% for August 2026) - REAL-terms growth since methodology v5.1, so a flat score of 5.0 means prices held their value against inflation. context.priceTrendPct is the cash trend, context.priceTrendRealPct the figure scored. Methodology v5.2 scales each tail against the real-terms fastest riser and steepest faller across ALL 97 boroughs in the sterling pool, not this city cohort - a city-sized cohort put one borough per city on each rail every month by construction. Growth is therefore comparable BETWEEN cities; context.growthRankInCity carries the within-city standing. No previous vintage exists for this city, so ?compare=previous declines rather than reporting zero change.
